To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency of IPMSM can be improved in electric vehicles by operating at minimum overall losses instead minimum current per torque in a large range of operation points.
the operation points in the torque and speed space, where the IPMSM can be operated most efficient, are dependent on the vehicle operation and therefore cannot be determined a priori.
the efficiency of an IPMSM can potentially be improved by operating the motor with minimum overall loss instead of minimum current for the torque requirement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new operation point selection method for IPMSMs in traction applications, which can potentially reduce losses and improve efficiency.
an efficient operation of IPMSM in drive trains of electrical and hybrid vehicles.
the question, if a torque control scheme can be improved to operate the motor at lower current and higher efficiency than a current control scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potential for an efficiency improvement by operating a motor at minimum overall losses instead at minimum current per torque can be expected in electric and hybrid vehicles.

the potential to reduce the overall losses in traction drive systems of electrical and hybrid vehicles by using a loss optimized operation point selection strategy can be realized in a wide range of operation points.
in most operation ranges, the efficiency can be improved by operating the motor with minimum overall loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the minimum overall losses operation point strategy can potentially reduce the losses and thus the power consumption and the fuel consumption in electric and hybrid electric vehicles.
the efficiency of the motor is improved in a significant amount by operating it at the minimum overall losses instead the minimum current per torque.
a minimum current control scheme can lead to a higher efficiency in the medium to high speed range of the motor, if the motor is operated with a constant current limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a minimum loss operation point selection strategy has the potential to increase the energy efficiency of traction drives.
a more complex operation point selection strategy can be beneficial for electric vehicles.
a minimum loss strategy is a good alternative to the minimum current strategy in the operation range of interest for electric and hybrid vehicles.
